content: My favorite part is not knowing if it's fully tightened or if i have more threads to cut in.

If you're doing the Gen 2 upgrade at the same time as the 4-tool upgrade, you've reached the next transition point to switch back to the overall guide for that process (2 steps earlier than those installing the 8-tool INDX)

Holes are too small to get threads to start. I used a 3/32 drill bit by hand and just enlarged the opening.

Then start the threads in each hole. Then assembly is easier.
Screw the M3x12cT screws in a few turns without the top first, then take them out. They will catch better when the top is on.
Beware !!!! the PTFE Tubes linkes you to the founders edition manual then all of a sudden your process is different???
holes in the 3d printed part are too small so screws wont catch, use a craft knife to countersink edge of the holes
Dear Prusa: Not every saves every little allen key/tool that came with their printer. If you're gonna require a long torx wrench, just include it!
A note should be here for the Gen 2 Upgrade
I had a power drill and ran the screw  1/2 way in and out 3 times to form the threads.  Then put the top on,  careful the screw gets hot.

worst part so far. I don't have a t10 screwdriver. been using an electric screwdriver so far but it doesn't fit that deep into the tiny hole. and these screws can't tap into this part. the only way this was even possible was to pre-drill the holes and use an uncomfortable allen key to force the screws in

Thank you for the comments about going back to the Gen2 upgrade.

I have the 4 tool option so I wouldn't have seen the reminder at step 52 because that's for the 8 tool conversion.

The note for the 4-tool version should say if you are doing the Gen 2 upgrade also, go to this page FIRST! https://help.prusa3d.com/article/assemblling-the-prusa-indx-core-one-with-the-gen-2-upgrade_1147602#mounting-the-side-panels-ptfe-and-right-cover
The holes in the plastic were too small for the screws, requiring a massive amount of force to get them in. :-(

replies.content: If that's the case (it was for me as well), you can increase a tiny bit the size of the top of the hole so the screw will engage. No need to apply much force afterward, the screw does the job itself.
